memberdef.definition: std::function<std::vector<Section*>(std::size_t group)> AGRemapCore::GraphCreate< K, V, KeyHash, KeyEqual >::sectionsOf
memberdef.name: sectionsOf

para.verbatim: embed:rst The `sections`_ of each group's graph, given the group's index -- set, the edit builds a graph from them for EVERY group present when it runs and adds it under \ref graphId's component and object (its ``iniIndex`` is unused), instead of adding \ref graph. **Borrowed**, read only while the edit runs. A section of a name already in the graph is left out, so the first one wins; a group handed no sections gets no graph. When there are no groups at all, group 0's sections go into a group of their own. This is how sections held in a :cpp:class:`GraphEditVariables` variable are written out as a graph in each group -- a fixer's own sections into its file and every copy. **Default**: unset

memberdef.definition: void AGRemapCore::BaseIniPartEdit::clear
memberdef.name: clear

para.verbatim:
embed:rst This class inherits from :cpp:class:`BaseIniGraphGroupEdit` Adds a graph to a group of graphs, under a graph id of the caller's choosing -- the counterpart of :cpp:class:`GraphRemove`, which takes one out :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Where :cpp:class:`GraphGroupRemap` produces its graphs by copying ones the group already holds, this one takes a graph the CALLER built and puts it in. That is what a fixer needs when the graph it wants to render is not a copy of anything the parser handed it .. note:: **The graph is BORROWED and deep-copied in.** :cpp:func:`IIniGraphGroups::addGraph` requires a graph the groups object already owns -- one that came out of its own :cpp:func:`IIniGraphGroups::getGraph`, :cpp:func:`IIniGraphGroups::removeGraph`, :cpp:func:`IIniGraphGroups::deepcopyGraph` or :cpp:func:`IIniGraphGroups::createGraph` -- because the groups own their graphs' lifetimes. So this edit hands \ref graph to :cpp:func:`IIniGraphGroups::deepcopyGraph` and adds the COPY, which leaves the caller owning what it passed and free to reuse it for several ids. Storing the caller's pointer directly would be a dangling reference the moment the caller's graph went out of scope .. note:: A \ref graphId whose ``iniIndex`` is past the end of the groups is skipped silently, as :cpp:class:`GraphRemove` skips an out-of-range id -- **except** for an index of exactly :cpp:func:`IIniGraphGroups::size`, which appends a fresh group and adds the graph to that. Appending the ONE group the index asks for is the useful case (a fix that renders an extra ``.ini`` file); growing the list to reach an arbitrary index is not, and an index far past the end is a caller's mistake rather than a request for thousands of empty groups .. note:: An existing graph already stored under \ref graphId is REPLACED, which is :cpp:func:`IIniGraphGroups::addGraph`'s own behaviour rather than anything this edit adds

The type of the values stored in a referenced :cpp:class:IfContentPart

An equality comparator for K. Defaults to std::equal_to<K>
